references.text: The parallel text in the Gospel of Matthew where Jesus says: "Do not think that I have come to bring peace on earth. I have not come to bring peace, but a sword." [ref:Matt 10:34-36|Matthew 10:34-36] expresses the same message about division, but uses the word "sword" instead of "division".

The prophet Micah describes how family bonds are broken: "For the son despises his father, the daughter rises up against her mother" ([ref:Mi 7:6|Micah 7:6]). Jesus refers directly to this prophecy in the following verses in Luke 12.

The immediate continuation in [ref:Luk 12:52-53|Luke 12:52-53] elaborates on what kind of division Jesus is speaking about: five in one house will be divided, three against two and two against three, and family members set against each other.

Simeon prophesied already when Jesus was presented in the temple that he was "set for the fall and rising again of many in Israel, and for a sign which shall be spoken against … that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed" ([ref:Luk 2:34-35|Luke 2:34-35]). Jesus' coming would inevitably create division.

In [ref:Joh 7:43|John 7:43] it is stated that there was division (σχίσμα) among the crowd because of Jesus. This shows that Jesus' presence and preaching actually led to division, as he himself predicted.
Also in [ref:Joh 9:16|John 9:16] division arose among the Pharisees because of Jesus, confirming that his coming brought division rather than outward peace.
In [ref:Joh 10:19|John 10:19] there was again division (σχίσμα) among the Jews because of Jesus' words, a recurring pattern that confirms Jesus' statement that he came to bring division.

Isaiah prophesies about the Prince of Peace ([ref:Jes 9:5-6|Isaiah 9:5-6]), but Jesus' words in Luke 12:51 clarify that final peace comes only after the division between those who accept him and those who reject him is complete.

In [ref:Matt 10:21-22|Matthew 10:21-22] Jesus says that "brother will betray brother … and you will be hated by all for my name's sake", which elaborates on the familial and social division that follows faith in him.
